summary: Not accepted yet. Provenance, frozen-schema preservation, typed response compatibility, and recorded checks are strong, but two validation gaps remain in the public model APIs.

findings.description: The four existing write models and GatewayMcpServersClientListOptions still route parse/build_validated through frozen schemas that reject tags. For example, McpIntegrationUpdateRequest::builder().tags(Patch::Null).build_validated(Mode::Request) fails although the corresponding client accepts that request. Tests exercise versioned standalone validators and serde construction, leaving this public construction path uncovered.
findings.required_fix: Generate tag-aware request validation for these model APIs while preserving the frozen standalone roots. Add parse and build_validated tests covering valid tags, null, omission, and invalid values across all five affected types.

findings.description: GatewayMcpServersClientListOptions serializes extensions["tags"] when its typed tags field is unset. A caller can supply the string "not json" or "{\"env\":1}" through the extension builder. The client's check_filter examines only query.tags, so it skips validation; the versioned schema accepts any string, and common::query forwards the invalid filter to authentication and transport.
findings.required_fix: Validate the effective serialized tags filter before authentication, including extension-supplied values, or reject this extension collision consistently. Add mocked wire tests asserting zero token-provider and transport calls for invalid extension-supplied filters.
